waveOwnership: new docs/specs/tests only; no runtime visual mutation

decisions.statement: Mazer's target product is the Fawxzzy Precision Arcade direction: a mobile-first, installable, precision-arcade maze game where the board is the hero and application chrome only explains, enables, or protects play.

Phaser owns world/maze simulation-facing presentation (board rendering, title path animation, world-space entities, camera/world effects, menu demonstration maze, world diagnostics). DOM owns application shell, forms, HUD, touch controls, settings, dialogs, guide/confirmations, and system chrome. Semantic tokens, state registry, commands, view models, responsive metrics, platform profiles, topology/path geometry, icon definitions, motion semantics, diagnostics schema, and capture IDs are shared contracts owned by neither renderer alone.

The shipping maze presentation remains connected corridors, not exposed square tiles. Tile topology stays canonical underlying data; visible square-tile boundaries are optional proof/debug treatment only, never the shipping default.
Mobile, desktop, TV, OBS, arcade, and cyberdeck are output profiles, not public themes. Profiles vary layout and density; they never vary brand identity.

One canonical player-facing theme (Fawxzzy Precision Arcade) replaces the public theme matrix. The noir, ember, vellum, aurora, and monolith theme variants are archived historical experiments, not live public options, and no public theme switch ships in the canonical product.
proof-surfaces.html and visual-proof.html remain internal verification tools (projection QA / critical internal verification), not public product, and are not release-gating core surfaces.

Watch Pass (watch-pass-setup.html, watch-pass-preview.html) remains an incubating companion product behind a feature boundary. watch-pass-paywall.html is a commerce prototype only; no production billing or entitlement claim is permitted until real billing exists.
planet3d.html is an isolated lab, explicitly excluded from core-v1 release acceptance.
future-phaser.html is slated for adapter-lesson extraction (its useful adapter contracts become tests) and then entrypoint retirement.

MenuScene.ts is decomposed through characterization and adapters across later waves, not replaced in one rewrite. A big-bang rewrite is rejected because PR #83 overlaps core ownership and mechanics are already proof-backed.

PR #83's listed collision paths (MenuScene.ts, menuRuntimeDiagnostics.ts, legacyAuth.ts, legacyPlayerMessage.ts, shared capture scripts, plus the always-protected vite.config.ts and package.json) are protected and single-owner until PR #83's disposition clears, to be reconciled via a separate later integrator-exclusive PR (Wave 0B), not any parallel lane including this one.

No source lane may claim the redesign complete until the final acceptance matrix (the nine-point Definition of Complete) passes and old duplicated UI paths are removed or formally retained with an owner and purpose.

Wave 0B (the integrator-exclusive reconciliation the `pr83-protected-paths-hold` decision names as the path to releasing PR #83's hold) is PR #131 (`claude/mazer-pr83-fitness-auth-parity-successor`), which merges PR #83's original, committed, Codex-reviewed intent (`codex/fitness-auth-capability-parity-20260717`, head `3eab0e3cc534d5a38edbcb7c72ceb99f3db48467`) into current `main`, with two narrow, hand-resolved conflicts (an additive MenuScene.ts import-block conflict, and a bottom-options-label test assertion updated to match main's own already-merged behavior). PR #83 is the branch this reconciliation supersedes and is intended to be closed as superseded once PR #131 merges; PR #83 itself was never commented on, pushed to, or otherwise modified as part of this reconciliation. `pr83-protected-paths-hold` is released for PR #131's own reconciled content ONLY: `prProtection.releases[]` records a release that is narrowly scoped by exact branch name (`grantedTo.successorBranch`) to PR #131's branch alone, and by exact path list (`releasedPaths`) to precisely the protected paths PR #131 actually touches. This release: (a) does NOT modify or shrink `prProtection.protectedPaths` itself -- every one of those 9 paths remains listed and remains protected for every branch other than PR #131's own; (b) does NOT cover `vite.config.ts`, which PR #131 does not touch and which stays fully protected everywhere, including on PR #131's own branch; (c) does NOT extend to PR #82 (`codex/fp-mzr-rec-001-supabase-source-recovery`) or to any branch other than PR #131's -- PR #82 touches only `package.json` among the protected paths, and that file's protection remains fully enforced for PR #82's branch, for `main`, and for every branch except PR #131's exact branch name; (d) is evaluated at check time by `scripts/check-decision-registry.mjs`'s `resolveCurrentGitBranch` + `resolveReleasedProtectedPaths` + `collectProtectedPathViolations(changedFiles, registry, { releasedPaths })`, not by disabling, skipping, or weakening the guard itself. A full, unconditional drop of these paths from `protectedPaths` (ending the hold for every branch, not just PR #131's) is deliberately left for a separate future step, to be taken only once PR #131 actually merges and PR #83 is closed as superseded -- this decision documents the interim, PR-131-scoped release only.

phaserOwns: world-space player, start, goal, trail, cues, and future Fragment entities

prProtection.note: protectedPaths is a snapshot of PR #83's file-ownership collision list (per blueprint/09_MIGRATION_WAVES_AND_PR_LANES.md file ownership guardrails) plus the always-protected vite.config.ts and package.json. Reconciliation is Wave 0B, integrator-exclusive, not this lane (0A has exclusiveFiles: [] per spec/pr-lanes.json). protectedPaths itself is intentionally left unchanged by the Wave 0B release below -- these paths remain protected in general, for every branch except the one specific release grants below.

additionalOwnershipGuardrails.note: Listed as a single-owner/integrator surface in blueprint/09_MIGRATION_WAVES_AND_PR_LANES.md's file ownership guardrails table, alongside the paths above. No concrete file exists yet -- Wave 1B (PR 1B, semantic tokens and cross-renderer consumption) is what creates it. Recorded here so the exact path can be added to protectedPaths the moment it exists, rather than the guardrail being silently dropped.

releases.scopeNote: Applies ONLY to commits on grantedTo.successorBranch, matched by exact string equality against the branch name scripts/check-decision-registry.mjs's resolveCurrentGitBranch() resolves at check time. Any other branch -- including main, PR #82's branch, and any future/unrelated branch that happens to touch one of releasedPaths -- gets zero release and the full protectedPaths violation still fires. vite.config.ts is deliberately excluded from releasedPaths: PR #131 does not touch it, so it stays protected even on PR #131's own branch. package.json IS included because PR #131 legitimately adds one new script entry (visual:auth-capabilities) alongside the already-protected capture scripts it wires up; this does not touch or authorize any of PR #82's separate, unrelated package.json changes, and PR #82's own branch remains fully subject to protectedPaths for package.json exactly as before this release existed.
